extracted.intended_audience: USPTO policymakers, patent examiners, and patent applicants/practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria concerning search and examination quality at the USPTO, including examiner behavior, applicant searching/IDS, third‑party submissions, tooling (open source indexing), incentives, supervision, and performance metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-office trust in search results (PPH effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners tend to trust the search and examination results of other examiners (e.g., under PPH) but place less reliance on the search results of applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize legal differences across jurisdictions in applying prior art, but leverage trust in other offices to improve efficiency; be aware of lower reliance on applicant searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worksharing / reuse of first‑filed office work
rubrics_metrics.description: Work by a patent office where a patent application is first filed (search and examination) should be taken advantage of by patent offices of second or later filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use earlier office's search/examination to focus resources on improving patent quality and reducing redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party search assistance (social media/wiki/bounties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable examiner posts/questions via social media/wiki to solicit voluntary peer assistance; consider incentives (bounties) for third parties to provide prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether voluntary 'peer to peer' is sufficient or if incentives are needed to increase useful prior art contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of search specialist examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve search efficiency and effectiveness by using search specialist examiners having state‑of‑the‑art technological knowledge and higher search engine/software expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy specialists for complex search tasks and cross‑discipline searches where advanced tools/techniques add value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner with private search firms
rubrics_metrics.description: PTO can partner with private search firms to improve search effectiveness and efficiency and obtain benefits of leading edge search strategies and techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outsource or collaborate to access advanced search methods, while considering cost/oversight concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer‑to‑Patent pilot observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Art found by Peer‑to‑Patent was rarely considered more relevant than examiner‑found art, though pilot reports may have guided examiners; scale‑up viability is unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate benefits beyond citation counts (e.g., guidance to examiner) and assess feasibility of scaling the pilot before broad adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement social media for examiner knowledge sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Emerging social media technologies could be implemented within the USPTO to improve knowledge sharing and collaboration among examiners and between examiners and patent agents/applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use platforms to share search techniques, reach remote examiners, and engage external communities; plan moderation and resource needs carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party submissions: timing and content requirements (Intellectual Ventures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow third parties to submit prior art any time after publication and before a notice of allowance (and in reexamination), conditional on (a) identifying the claim elements each reference is relevant to, and (b) identifying specific wording/figures in the prior art relevant to each claim element (not merely whole claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid examiner/applicant burden, disallow arguments or permit only minimal explanations pointing to relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open source software (OSS) prior art indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Index and archive public OSS project websites (e.g., SourceForge) in a form that efficiently stores indexes to source code and documentation for specific dates to enable date‑specific prior art identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take advantage of revision control systems (e.g., Subversion) to identify state of code at given dates; enable examiner searches by priority date and architectural keywords.

rubrics_metrics.name: OSAPA / tools for OSS prior art identification (IBM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop search tools (like OSAPA) that use publicly available search engines and OSS repositories to identify open source software that may be valuable prior art against software patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with developers and the open source community to build tools that surface relevant non‑patent literature (source code) to examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of Information Disclosure Statements (IDS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Question whether IDS aids examiner search; why examiners may not utilize IDS as basis for their search (time/credit concerns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate whether IDS reduces pendency and whether examiners read IDS references; consider structural incentives or systems changes if IDS is underutilized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 56 (IDS) scope reform proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider changing Rule 56 to limit IDS to 'non public' prior art and create incentives to disclose non‑public prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh benefits of narrowing IDS to meaningful undisclosed art versus the risk of discouraging disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and education on searching (examiners & applicants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand training and education for examiners and applicants on searching and search strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide online training, best practices, and access to databases/techniques to improve applicant searches and examiner confidence in applicant‑provided searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner independent search practice vs reading applicant IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Question whether 'independent search' is interpreted to preclude examiners from reading IDS prior to their search and whether that practice reduces efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify expectations: allow examiners to review applicant searches (IDS) before their own search where appropriate and adjust performance accounting if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant pre‑filing searches improve application quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants' knowledge of closest prior art before filing results in improved patent applications with clearer claim scope and reduced pendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incentivize pre‑filing searches and enable applicants to draft claims with better distinction from prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentives for applicant pre‑filing searching
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide incentives (e.g., accelerate examination for those conducting searches; a check box on application transmittal to indicate a pre‑filing search) without requiring characterization of prior art or disclosure of search strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance incentives with fears of inequitable conduct; avoid requiring characterization that increases litigation risk for applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create best practice search documents / wiki for applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop best practice and 'how‑to' articles or an internal/external wiki with search procedures by class to help applicants perform initial patent searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use incentives for examiner contributions; consider hosted third‑party community resources (e.g., Intellogist) rather than building a heavy USPTO forum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand PAIR capability to search multiple file histories
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow searching more than a single PAIR record at a time to improve public access to prosecution histories and facilitate comparative searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lifting this restriction would aid practitioners and public research into prosecution patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial/expedite incentives tied to applicant‑identified art
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider financial credit against patent fees or expedited examination for applicants who conduct pre‑filing searches or who identify more relevant prior art after an examiner's search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design incentive mechanisms that compensate applicants for litigation risk and encourage meaningful pre‑filing searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty suggestion for low‑quality patents (comment)
rubrics_metrics.description: A comment suggested imposing a penalty fee for patent requesters whose patents are rejected or revoked as anticipated by prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a proposed deterrent; consider fairness, litigation uncertainty, and potential chilling effects on filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequitable conduct doctrine disincentivizes applicant cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Current inequitable conduct doctrine (as developed by case law) discourages applicants from explaining submissions or characterizing prior art for fear of misrepresentation and excessive disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider statutory remedies or policy changes to reduce unpredictability and encourage constructive applicant disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide public/electronic access to PTO search tools (WEST/EAST)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide inventors and the public electronic access to the same search facilities examiners use (WEST/EAST) over the Internet and partner with multiple search providers to make information available for free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opening examiner tools to the public could improve applicant searching and transparency; address licensing and privacy concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage early third‑party prior art submissions and credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage third‑party prior art submission early with incentives; consider assignee filing and small/micro entity designations for financial credits for third‑party submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design mechanisms to give credit/rewards for useful early prior art contributions while preventing abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners should read entire IDS and specification before search
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should read all prior art references in the IDS and the entire specification — not just claims — before conducting a search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether current time and count systems are commensurate with this expectation and adjust examiner accounting if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use post‑grant outcomes as examiner feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Use litigation, opposition, and reexamination results as feedback to examiners and include positive and negative outcomes in performance measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate downstream validity outcomes into performance evaluation where appropriate and with due regard to context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure search gaps using QIR data
rubrics_metrics.description: Use PTO QIR (Quality Index Review) data to measure time for search vs. results and identify search gaps potentially attributable to application technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze QIR metrics by tech center to target training and process improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentives for high‑quality examination and compact prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide incentives (beyond production bonuses) to encourage examiners to follow Compact Prosecution, issue relevant and meaningful office actions rapidly, identify patentable subject matter early, and provide timely/complete responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create and measure high examination quality metrics and align incentives accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑search interview between applicant and assigned examiner (3M)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permit applicants to conduct an interview with the assigned examiner after the examiner has read the application but prior to any search, limited to mutual understanding of claim term interpretation for search and prosecution scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require a pre‑search interview summary; allow filing claim amendments resulting from the interview; restrict patentability discussion under 35 U.S.C. 102/103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide examiner search report to applicant before first Office Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide applicants with an examiner search report indicating relevance of the closest prior art before the first office action; move IDS requirement to follow the search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow applicants to submit an IDS and schedule a pre‑first O/A teleconference to discuss relevancy; consider financial credit if applicants later identify more relevant art than the examiner reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify count system to credit pre‑OA interview/search activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify examiner count system to give credit for pre‑first O/A interviews and pre‑search activities to encourage early engagement that reduces overall pendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align productivity accounting to reward front‑loaded, quality‑improving work rather than only downstream production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate requirement for applicants to cite patent literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate the requirement for applicants to dump patent references on examiners, since examiners are generally better at finding the most relevant patent literature while applicants are better at finding non‑patent literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow each party to focus on their strengths; applicants still provide the most relevant patent references they have identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality examination: proper interpretation and application of closest prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality examination requires the proper interpretation and application of the closest prior art to the claims and clear statements for rejection and allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure rejections/allowances include technical reasoning, not mere word matches; provide standards to interpret claim terms and articulate technical basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on first Office Action on the merits (compact prosecution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review and improve first office actions: cite the best references and make the best rejections immediately; enforce Compact Prosecution and 37 CFR 1.104(c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor first OA quality, increase front‑end credits, and reduce later stage credits to encourage getting it right early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection/allowance must explain technical reasoning (no conclusory statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejection and allowance must explain the examiner’s technical reasoning; conclusory, unsupported statements are unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require detailed explanation linking claim elements to prior art and technical rationale for conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for citing portions of references and detailed citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Create standards for examiners to identify portions of cited references that are relevant, and in office actions provide specific citations indicating which elements in cited references correspond to each claim term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces ambiguity (e.g., whether identical wording is used for identical/different purposes) and helps applicants understand examiner positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow claims once objections/rejections are overcome (do it right once)
rubrics_metrics.description: If rejection and objections are overcome, claims should be allowed and not subjected to another search and application of new prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit repetitive searching/applying new art after objections resolved to reduce pendency and improve predictability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject inadequately described claims and require antecedent basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject claims that are inadequately described; require antecedent basis for amended claims and encourage active amendment suggestions by examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote clear claim drafting and examiner assistance to guide applicants toward allowable claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review of first office actions for quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement panel review of at least a percentage of first office actions (particularly from non‑primary examiners) to improve first OA quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel review increases thoroughness and produces higher quality first OAs, reducing pendency and encouraging better examiner work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical accuracy and avoid word‑matching without technical explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Finding the closest art does not mean it is properly understood or applied; the cited reference must actually disclose or suggest the claim limitation and not be relied on solely due to word matching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify improper instances of superficial word matching; require technical explanation for why a reference meets a limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ombudsman pilot: access, transparency, and metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance Ombudsman pilot: make public the issues the Ombudsman can address, provide an avenue for further pursuit if applicants dissatisfied, and establish a public database tracking issues and outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use metrics like number/types of requests, time to resolution, customer surveys, and long‑term processing time changes (broken down by Technology Center) to evaluate efficacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: External technical advisory board / consultation mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider formation of an external technical advisory board for examiner consultation to aid understanding of complex technical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use outside experts to improve technical accuracy where internal resources are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge varying application complexity and adjust resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all applications are equal; develop objective criteria to categorize applications by complexity and allow differing examiner time allotments and counts accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria may include technology, specification length, number of examples, references cited, and claim scope; permit applicant petition and examiner interview regarding category assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism for applicants to address examiner performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop mechanisms for applicants to raise concerns about examiner performance without risk of negative consequences and for targeted management attention/training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track anomalous activities and provide targeted training; use Ombudsman and other channels while avoiding punitive misuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase use of MPEP citations and improve 35 U.S.C. 103 guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve guidance and references used in prosecution by increasing MPEP case citations and clarifying 35 U.S.C. 103 guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Better citation and guidance help consistency across examiners and tech centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: English proficiency for examiners and QIR evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: All U.S. examiners must be able to communicate clearly in English; QIR data should evaluate examiners for whom English is their second language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clear file histories and communications; use QIR to identify training needs rather than public shaming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiered examination based on objective complexity criteria (GSK)
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate applications by objective criteria (technology, spec length, working examples, references, claim scope) into tiers (e.g., 1 high complexity, 3 low) and allocate counts/time accordingly; allow applicant petition and interview for category assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust application fees for more complex cases and provide sufficient examiner time to perform comprehensive searches for complex applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisory review responsibility and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervisors should actively review O/As, restriction requirements, final rejections, allowances and appeal answers; track improper rejections identified by supervisors for use in examiner performance review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish who reviews supervisors; include supervisor metrics in performance evaluations; ensure supervisors are actually supervising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish standards for Quality Review and focus on outliers
rubrics_metrics.description: PTO should publish the standards used for Quality Review, use QIR to focus on outliers, initiate quality review after first O/A and after first O/A following RCE, and reduce use of form paragraph rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency in standards helps applicants understand expectations and supports targeted training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand examiner training (e.g., 102(e), PCT unity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand training for examiners on topics such as 102(e) and PCT unity of invention and other substantive/practical examination topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide both formal and informal mentoring; address training gaps exacerbated by remote/hotelling arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish and publish examiner & supervisor performance metrics and reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish/publish performance review metrics, conduct annual performance reviews per standards, rank examiners and supervisors by performance as well as production, and address issues promptly; include mentoring programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use QIR data confidentially for constructive feedback; avoid punitive misuse except in extreme cases; incentivize experienced examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring and retention for remote/hotelling examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement mentoring programs for remote/hotelling examiners to maintain training quality and informal mentoring interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide merit‑based incentives to experienced examiners and ensure junior examiners receive sufficient informal training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism to address attorney/agent performance quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop mechanisms to assess and address the performance quality of patent attorneys and agents in preparing and prosecuting patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the role of counsel in patent quality; create feedback or remediation tools where counsel performance adversely affects prosecution or enforceability.
